generic_sampling_rules.int_primary_key: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL; generated before any child FK is drawn.
generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key: Copy an existing parent primary-key value from the final surviving parent PK set; for nullable FKs include NULL rows and rows referencing parents that have no children; never NULL a NOT NULL or PK-member FK column.
generic_sampling_rules.int_quantity: Non-negative integer; sample from a small pool including 0, 1, 2, 3 and a few larger values.
generic_sampling_rules.int_rank: Positive integer 1..N; sample from a small pool including 1, 2, 3.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Random short alphabetic string; occasionally reuse an existing value to create duplicates (20-50% duplicate share on DISTINCT columns).
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Pick uniformly from the column's enum list.
generic_sampling_rules.text_generic: Random short alphabetic string; allow near-duplicate variants (case changes, trailing spaces) when no constraint forbids it.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For every nullable column, at least one NULL row per instance; NULL share follows the compact database (0% observed, so keep NULLs sparse, ~5-10%); planted NULLs are applied after all other post-processing and never on NOT NULL or PK columns.

issues.evidence: writer.write_instance_sqlite is called from cli._one as write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p) with no orig_path argument, so it takes the fallback branch that creates an empty DDL clone instead of copying the compact database. Execution feedback confirms this: validity.reasons.compact_rows_missing = 20/20 and no_rows_added = 6. The docstring and instance.py both claim 'every instance is a copy of the compact database plus appended rows', but the code path never copies it.
issues.requested_revision: Pass orig_path through cli._one (e.g. write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p, orig_path=a['orig'])) so the compact DB is actually copied, or make orig_path a required argument. Verify that compact_rows_missing drops to 0 in the next run.

issues.evidence: integrity.fk_violations = 211 across 20 instances, and validity.reasons.new_integrity_failures = 20/20. Root causes visible in code: (a) instance.build_random_instance calls fill_foreign_keys_consistently before the parent table's generated PKs are guaranteed to survive sample_fresh_primary_keys / drop_unique_duplicates, so child FKs can reference PKs that were later dropped; (b) _ensure_unmatched_parents sets child FK values to None on columns like player_coach.Player_ID and coach.Club_ID, but player_coach.Player_ID is part of the composite PK (NOT NULL) and coach.Club_ID is a NOT NULL FK in the schema — this both violates NOT NULL and breaks the FK; (c) _plant_nulls is applied to every nullable column including FK columns (e.g. coach.Club_ID, player_coach.Player_ID) after FK consistency was established, so planted NULLs on NOT NULL FK columns break integrity; (d) writer disables foreign_keys=OFF during insert, so violations are not caught at write time.
issues.requested_revision: Fix FK generation order: generate parent PKs first, then draw child FKs only from the final surviving parent PK set. Do not plant NULLs on columns that are NOT NULL or part of a PK (player_coach.Player_ID, coach.Club_ID). Do not set NOT NULL FK columns to NULL in _ensure_unmatched_parents; instead ensure unmatched parents by leaving at least one parent unreferenced (which is already possible without nulling). Re-enable foreign_keys=ON during insert (or run a post-write PRAGMA foreign_key_check) so violations surface. Target fk_violations = 0.

issues.evidence: The NULL rule requires 'for every nullable column ... each instance contains generated rows with NULL and rows with non-NULL values'. Execution feedback shows coach.Club_ID: NULL 0/8 and player.Rank: NULL 0/12 — both nullable columns with zero NULLs. This is because _plant_nulls is skipped for FK columns (they are filled by fill_foreign_keys_consistently and then _ensure_unmatched_parents may null them, but only for the two UNMATCHED targets) and because player.Rank is not in any sampler path that plants NULLs (it is not in ENUMS/RANGES/DUP_SHARE/GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS, so it falls through to make_column_sampler, and _plant_nulls is applied — but the feedback shows 0 NULLs, indicating the column is being overwritten or the sampler path bypasses it).
issues.requested_revision: Ensure _plant_nulls is applied to every nullable column after all other post-processing, including FK columns that are nullable (coach.Club_ID is nullable in the schema but is a FK — it must receive NULLs per the interface rule). For player.Rank, trace why _plant_nulls produces 0 NULLs (likely the column is regenerated or the sampler returns non-NULL after planting) and fix. Per instruction 7 this is a note, not a blocker, but it should be corrected.

issues.evidence: The specification's null_targets lists player_coach.Player_ID and coach.Club_ID as columns that should receive NULLs, but player_coach.Player_ID is part of the composite PRIMARY KEY (Player_ID, Coach_ID) and is therefore NOT NULL by SQLite semantics. The spec's own per_column_exceptions entry for player_coach.Player_ID says 'null_share: none (NOT NULL column)', contradicting null_targets. This inconsistency drives the engineer's _ensure_unmatched_parents to null a PK column.
issues.requested_revision: Remove player_coach.Player_ID from null_targets (it is NOT NULL). Keep coach.Club_ID as a nullable FK target. Clarify that unmatched-join targets for player_coach.Player_ID must be achieved by leaving a parent player unreferenced, not by nulling the child PK.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions include coach.Coach_ID with pattern duplicates_for_distinct (duplicate_share 20-50%), but coach.Coach_ID is the PRIMARY KEY of coach and is generated by _fresh_pk_values as sequential unique integers. A PK cannot have duplicates. Similarly player.Gender duplicates_for_distinct is listed but Gender is an enum with only two values, so 'duplicate share' is trivially satisfied but the target is meaningless as a distinctness constraint.
issues.requested_revision: Remove coach.Coach_ID from DUP_SHARE / per_column_exceptions (PK columns cannot have duplicates). Reconsider whether player.Gender needs a duplicate-share target given its two-value domain.

issues.evidence: instance.choose_table_sizes applies jitter rng.randint(-2, 2) to spec.TABLE_SIZES, so table sizes deviate from the specification's table_sizes_per_instance (e.g. player 14 ± 2). The spec gives exact sizes; the program silently perturbs them. Additionally, _ensure_ties forces vals[1] = vals[0] on match_result.Club_ID, which can create a duplicate (Rank, Club_ID) PK pair if the two rows share the same Rank — this is a latent PK-duplicate risk (currently pk_duplicates=0 only because Rank values happen to differ).
issues.requested_revision: Either honor spec.TABLE_SIZES exactly (remove jitter) or document the jitter as an intentional deviation in the spec. For _ensure_ties, ensure the two rows being tied have distinct Rank values so the composite PK (Rank, Club_ID) is not violated.
